text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Trade and Industry Minister Jassem al-Mudaf says a committee will study a proposed law aimed at attracting foreign investments.
- No one is above the law, Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al- Ahmad al-Sabah told local newspaper editors on Monday.

- Interior Minister Sheikh Mohammad Khaled al-Sabah to present parliament on Tuesday with details on the assassination attempt against Abdullah al-Naibari. The liberal MP was shot twice in the Friday evening attack.
- Bahrain arrests Kuwaiti wanted for writing bad cheques.

- Finance Minister Nasser Rodhan tells newspaper editors main suspect in Naibari case has ties with him and with other ministers and senior officials. He was responding to rumours on his possible resignation.
- MPs demand cabinet reshuffle after Naibari attempt.
- Islamic banking services managing 30 percent of Gulf Arab savings.
- Naibari's condition improving, hospital says. Oxford- educated Naibari was hit in the jaw and shoulder. His wife suffered a superficial bullet wound.
